summary.en: Militants in Manipur ambushed vehicles on the Imphal-Ukhrul highway, killing four travelers and prompting security forces to launch search operations, while suspected militants fired at two cars in Ukhrul, killing four more. In Kangpokpi district a woman farmer was killed and three men wounded during a separate incident, and a bandh over a Kuki woman’s killing disrupted normal life. In Kashmir police, army and CRPF conducted a joint security mock drill in Bandipora’s Hajin area and placed forces on high alert after two SPOs were killed in Kishtwar. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militante i Manipur overfalt kjøretøy på Imphal-Ukhrul-veien, drepte fire reisende og førte til at sikkerhetsstyrker igangsatte søkeoperasjoner, mens mistenkte militante skjøt mot to biler i Ukhrul, og drepte fire til. I Kangpokpi-distrikt ble en kvinnelig bonde drept og tre menn såret i en separat hendelse, og en streik over drapet på en Kuki-kvinne forstyrret normallivet. I Kashmir gjennomførte politi, hær og CRPF en felles sikkerhetsøvelse i Bandiporas Hajin-område og satte styrker på høy beredskap etter at to SPO-er ble drept i Kishtwar. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
